implementerProof.how: Review round 5's change is two things in the evictor (006069a2): the re-arm of a room whose re-examination reached no verdict now backs off per attempt in a row, and a write of this process still in flight is an attempt rather than a verdict. Both are pinned by rows of the implementer's, and I drove the control for each myself — flattening the backoff to one interval, and turning the in-flight branch back into a verdict — rather than taking either from its report. The evictor rows ran four consecutive times green here, the whole two-process package and the browser suite were re-taken at this head, and CI's every lane is green at the code head f37678f7, which also clears the red the last round carried.
implementerProof.whatTheProofDidNotCover: The same boundary as last round, unchanged: neither of these two paths can be induced from outside the process. The in-flight branch needs a write of that process held between its operations, and the backoff needs a re-examination that keeps getting no answer; both are reached at seams inside the service, and an induction from outside (terminating the database's backends) also forces the listener's redial, whose reconnect sweep reaches the same outcome by another path. So both rest on the package rows at their seams plus my controls against them, and not on a two-process drive.
